title: The First American Mann Ki Baat
premise: What if Narendra Modi became president of the USA?
styleReason: Reference 08 mixes stylized 3D character scenes with abrupt red/black kinetic words and a bright end card; those devices make the jokes visual while the new story stays original.

story.goal: Address a new country with a confident first broadcast.
story.obstacle: The audience and fifty states expect to speak back.
story.turn: The competing questions overwhelm the one-way broadcast, so the microphone turns around.
story.payoff: A fictional America Ki Baat becomes a two-way show.

sources.claim: Mann Ki Baat is Modi's monthly radio programme.
sources.use: Name motif and fictional broadcast reversal.

sources.claim: Modi used dry humor about congressional harmony and yoga in a U.S. Congress speech.
sources.use: Checked his own humor; omitted from the short to preserve one story spine.

sources.claim: Mitron became an object of public jokes around Modi's speeches.
sources.use: Source motif for a new group-chat punch line.

sources.claim: Public memes have played on Modi's hugs with world leaders.
sources.use: Source motif for the meeting-clock escalation.

sources.claim: The U.S. president gives a State of the Union address.
Article II specifies natural-born-citizen eligibility for the U.S. presidency.
sources.use: Marks this premise as alternate-universe fiction.

jokes.setup: He opens a speech with Mitron.
jokes.originalPunch: The press room checks whether it joined a group chat.

jokes.setup: A diplomatic summit needs to start.
jokes.originalPunch: The greeting line consumes the entire meeting clock.
jokes.storyUse: Escalates the broadcast problem into physical comedy.

jokes.setup: One microphone cannot answer fifty states.
jokes.originalPunch: The show becomes America Ki Baat when he points it at the crowd.
jokes.storyUse: Resolves the conflict and closes the running gag.

beats.voice: America has a State of the Union. In this alternate universe, it gets Mann Ki Baat.
beats.visual: Stylized 3D White House press room; visible FICTIONAL SATIRE label; giant crimson programme card.
beats.motion: Push toward podium, snap to type card.
beats.caption: State of the Union / Mann Ki Baat

beats.voice: Modi walks in, says Mitron, and half the press room checks its group chats.
beats.visual: Cartoonlike Modi figure enters; reporter phones light up; black/red keyword card.
beats.motion: Follow entrance, then quick phone-light cascade and reaction cuts.
beats.caption: MITRON / GROUP CHAT?
beats.sound: Phone pings after the word; half-beat reaction.

beats.voice: At the summit, he greets every leader with a hug. The meeting clock does not survive.
beats.visual: 3D greeting line and giant clock; no real foreign leader likeness required.
beats.motion: Readable repeated greeting poses, then clock hands race.
beats.caption: THE MEETING CLOCK
beats.sound: Footsteps, quick clock ticks, restrained comic hit.

beats.voice: His cabinet brings fifty questions from fifty states. He brings one microphone.
beats.visual: Question cards stack in the 3D room; cut to a lone microphone on black.
beats.motion: Cards arrive in rhythm; hard isolate on microphone.
beats.caption: FIFTY QUESTIONS / ONE MIC
beats.sound: Paper hits; music ducks at one microphone.
beats.purpose: State the problem in one visual contrast.

beats.voice: Then every state talks at once. Suddenly, the broadcast has no host.
beats.visual: Fifty stylized speech bubbles crowd a red void; podium shrinks.
beats.motion: Speech bubbles multiply, then one abrupt collapse to near black.
beats.caption: EVERY STATE AT ONCE
beats.sound: Brief layered chatter, hard cut to near-silence.

beats.voice: He turns the microphone around. For the first time, he listens.
beats.visual: Close hand turns microphone toward a diverse cartoon crowd; wide room settles.
beats.motion: One clear physical rotation, then slow pullback.
beats.caption: HE LISTENS
beats.sound: One mic click; music opens gently.

beats.voice: Episode two is America Ki Baat. The comments are open.
beats.visual: Bright cyan end card in reference-08 grammar; fictional show title and comment icon.
beats.motion: Title lands once; clean end cut.
beats.caption: AMERICA KI BAAT · FICTIONAL SATIRE
beats.purpose: Pay off the running broadcast joke without an unrelated ad.
